title: Scaffold the Laravel application
user_visible_behavior: A developer can start the Laravel app locally and receive a successful response from its health endpoint.
verification: php artisan --version succeeds in the Laravel app directory
The app boots and GET /up (or equivalent health route) returns HTTP 200
The Laravel test suite runs (php artisan test)
evidence: php -v -> PHP 8.4.8 (cli, ZTS Visual C++ 2022 x64)
php artisan test -> 2 passed (2 assertions), exit 0
php artisan migrate --force -> users/cache/jobs framework tables migrated (SQLite)
serve smoke on port 8124 -> GET /up 200, GET / 200; server and child process stopped
init.ps1 (PowerShell gate) -> exit 0 (runs artisan --version + artisan test, starts no server)
notes: Scaffolded latest Laravel 13.x at repo root via temp dir + selective copy (--no-scripts). Framework migrations only; domain schema deferred to db-schema-market-data. init.ps1 is now a real non-blocking gate. See docs/specs/repo-scaffold-laravel.md, CONSTRAINTS.md.

title: Scaffold the React SPA
user_visible_behavior: A developer can build and start the React SPA and see a placeholder page styled with the AlphaPulse Tailwind tokens.
verification: npm install and npm run build succeed
The dev server serves a placeholder page that loads the DESIGN.md token stylesheet
Type checking / lint runs clean
notes: Reuse alphapulse/ only as a visual reference; do not ship its Express server or seeded data. See DESIGN.md.

title: Build the app shell and navigation
user_visible_behavior: A user sees the AlphaPulse header, EOD status, primary action and tab navigation (Screener, Chart, Admin, Portal) with the design tokens applied.
verification: Header and tab bar render per DESIGN.md (2px borders, hard shadows, accent button, mono metrics)
Tabs switch the active surface without a full reload
Layout is usable at desktop and tablet widths
notes: Visual source of truth is DESIGN.md and the alphapulse/ prototype. Copilot tab is out of MVP scope, do not add it.

title: Scaffold the Python engine
user_visible_behavior: A developer can run the Python engine locally and get a healthy response.
verification: The engine starts from a virtual environment
A health check (endpoint or CLI command) reports success
The test runner executes an initial test
notes: Owns scraping, indicator computation and signal detection. See docs/technical-discovery.md for the Laravel <-> engine boundary open question.

title: Create the market-data database schema
user_visible_behavior: Migrations create and roll back the tables for instruments, universes, daily bars, indicator snapshots and signals.
verification: Migrations run and roll back cleanly
Daily bars are unique per (instrument, date)
A test persists and reads back one instrument with one bar, one snapshot and one signal
notes: Entities and relationships are defined in docs/domain-model.md.

title: Register and log in a user
user_visible_behavior: A Visitor can create an account and sign in, and receives an authenticated session.
verification: Registration validates input and creates a user
Login with valid credentials returns an authenticated session; invalid credentials fail
Logout revokes the session
notes: See docs/user-and-access-model.md. Email verification depth is an implementation-time question.

title: Enforce admin role server-side
user_visible_behavior: Admin-only endpoints reject non-admin users, regardless of the UI.
verification: A registered non-admin receives 403 on an admin-only route
An admin account reaches the admin-only route
A test covers both cases
notes: Admin is granted out of band (seed/manual), never self-service. See docs/user-and-access-model.md.

title: Seed the S&P 500 universe
user_visible_behavior: The S&P 500 universe is populated with instruments carrying ticker, company, sector and exchange.
verification: Seeding creates the S&P 500 universe and its instruments
Instrument counts and a spot-checked ticker match the source list
Re-seeding does not duplicate instruments
notes: Constituent-list source and refresh cadence are implementation-time questions (docs/risks-and-open-questions.md).

title: Scrape EOD bars for one instrument
user_visible_behavior: The engine fetches one instrument's end-of-day OHLCV from the public source and stores its daily bars.
verification: A single-ticker fetch stores correctly parsed OHLCV bars
Re-running does not duplicate the same bar date (upsert)
Parsing is tested against a saved fixture, not only live network
notes: Data source and its legality are a blocking open question; treat live scraping as an integration concern.

title: Orchestrate a full Ingestion Run
user_visible_behavior: An Ingestion Run processes the whole universe and records an overall status plus per-instrument success or failure.
verification: A run over a fixture universe reaches completed and stores its results
A forced per-ticker failure yields a partial run with the failure recorded, not a crash
One run can be re-run for the failed instruments
notes: Implements the queued -> running -> completed/failed/partial lifecycle in docs/domain-model.md.

title: Compute indicator snapshots
user_visible_behavior: The engine computes and stores indicator snapshots (SMA/EMA, RSI, MACD, ADX, Bollinger, RVOL) for each stored daily bar.
verification: Computed indicators match hand-calculated fixtures for a small set of tickers
Instruments with insufficient history are flagged rather than producing wrong values
Snapshots are reproducible from stored bars without network access
notes: Exact indicator parameters are an implementation-time question; fixtures are the source of correctness.

title: Detect deterministic signals
user_visible_behavior: The engine stores deterministic signals per instrument: moving-average crosses, trend/MA alignment, breakout with RVOL, RSI and MACD conditions.
verification: Each signal rule has a fixture test for positive and negative cases
Signals are date-stamped and recomputed per Ingestion Run
A signal that no longer holds disappears on the next run
notes: MVP uses deterministic Signals only; geometric chartist patterns are later scope (docs/build-brief.md).

title: Schedule the daily EOD ingestion
user_visible_behavior: An Ingestion Run executes automatically after Market Close on trading days.
verification: The scheduler triggers a run after the configured close time
The schedule is DST-aware and skips non-trading days
A missed run can still be triggered manually
notes: Scheduling across DST and US market holidays is an implementation-time question.

title: Admin panel to control ingestion
user_visible_behavior: An Admin triggers or re-runs an Ingestion Run and sees status, telemetry and the run log.
verification: Admin can trigger a run and see it move through queued/running/completed
Admin can re-run failed instruments
The log stream shows per-instrument results; non-admins are denied
notes: Mirrors the admin surface in the alphapulse prototype, but only for real runs/logs.

title: Expose instrument detail API
user_visible_behavior: An API response provides an instrument's daily bars plus its latest snapshot and signals.
verification: GET of an instrument returns ordered bars, latest indicators and active signals
An unknown ticker returns a not-found response
Response shape is covered by a test
notes: Backs the chart screen. Keep payloads bounded for responsive charts.

title: Expose the screener API
user_visible_behavior: An API applies multi-criteria technical filters over the universe and returns a ranked candidate list.
verification: Filters (pattern/signal, RSI range, min RVOL, price above SMA200, MA cross) narrow results correctly on fixtures
Supported sort orders change the ranking
An empty result returns an empty list, not an error
notes: Filter set comes from FilterState in the alphapulse prototype; implement only MVP-relevant filters.

title: Screener filter UI
user_visible_behavior: A Visitor sets technical filters and receives a candidate list from the screener API.
verification: Changing filters issues a refreshed request and updates the list
Loading and empty states are visible
The filter controls follow DESIGN.md
notes: Anonymous browsing must work without login (docs/user-and-access-model.md).

title: Rank and sort the candidate list
user_visible_behavior: A user sorts the candidate list by RVOL, confidence/signal strength, RSI or change, and the ranking updates.
verification: Each supported sort order reorders the visible list consistently
Sorting is reflected in the API request, not only client-side
The selected sort persists while filters change
notes: Keep sort options limited to those the screener API supports.

title: Interactive candidate chart
user_visible_behavior: A user opens a candidate and sees an interactive candlestick chart with moving averages, volume and the signal's pivot/stop/target levels.
verification: The chart renders price, volume and MA overlays from the detail API
Signal reference levels are drawn from the instrument's active signal
The chart handles a ticker with insufficient history gracefully
notes: Charting library choice is a blocking open question (TradingView Lightweight Charts vs embedded widget).

title: Manage a personal watchlist
user_visible_behavior: A Registered User adds and removes instruments from their own watchlist and sees its current entries.
verification: Adding and removing an instrument updates the user's watchlist
A user cannot see or modify another user's watchlist
Anonymous access redirects to sign-in
notes: Ownership boundaries are defined in docs/user-and-access-model.md.

title: Save and re-apply screeners
user_visible_behavior: A Registered User saves the current filter set as a named Screener and re-applies it later.
verification: Saving persists the filter definition under the user's ownership
Applying a saved Screener restores its filters and results
A second user cannot read or delete the first user's Screener
notes: Implements the Saved Screener lifecycle in docs/domain-model.md.

title: User portal for screeners and watchlist
user_visible_behavior: A Registered User sees and manages their saved Screeners and watchlist in one place.
verification: The portal lists the user's saved Screeners and watchlist entries
Deleting a Screener removes it from the list
Only the owner's data is shown
notes: The mockup also shows a decorative PRO plan and P&L; those are explicitly out of scope.

title: Enforce anonymous vs registered access
user_visible_behavior: Anonymous visitors can browse the screener and charts, while saving screeners, editing the watchlist and admin actions require authentication and enforce ownership.
verification: Anonymous browse of screener and chart works
Protected actions require auth and redirect anonymous users
Ownership is enforced server-side for every owned resource
notes: Consolidates the access rules in docs/user-and-access-model.md into enforced behavior.
